evidence: The PR deleted `cli._status` while drift.py's `of()` docstring still named it; the agent deleted the cross-module name instead of repointing it to `chrome._reachability` as suggested, which removes the stale reference without creating a new one that can rot.
guidance_note: When a diff deletes or renames a symbol, grep the whole repo for the old name, docstrings included, before pushing.

evidence: `list_cmd`/`config_cmd` now reach `chrome._probe_port` and real sockets while `CliTest.setUp` stubbed only `scan`/`port_is_free`; the agent's poisoned-socket run showed 87 failures without the stub, and its reply admits it "noticed and wrongly deferred" the gap.
guidance_note: When a change adds a new external-system call under code the CLI tests exercise, add its stub to the shared setUp beside the existing external stubs in the same commit.

narrative: Two round-0 findings, both real and both from the original diff: a docstring naming the deleted `cli._status`, and an unstubbed socket probe in the CLI tests. The agent fixed both in one commit, deleting the stale cross-reference rather than repointing it, and verified the stub by poisoning `socket.create_connection`. Round 1 approved with no new findings.
guidance_observations: The agent had noticed the unmocked probe before review and deferred it; acting on a self-noticed gap would have avoided the finding.
Both fixes went out in one push, so review needed only one confirming round.

evidence: The `_Unasked` docstring said "`wait_for_cdp` puts the question unconditionally" and the agent confirmed `wait_for_cdp` "exists nowhere in this repo"; the function is `_await_startup`.
guidance_note: Before committing a docstring that names a function, grep for that symbol; a name written from memory must be confirmed to exist.

evidence: The literal five-command tuple was a real second copy of the click command set and was replaced with `_commands_offering_no_probe()` derived from click. The README-parsing half was declined because of an owner instruction against new tests that read README prose; the click enumeration already supplies the single source.
guidance_note: When a test enumerates commands that carry a decorator, derive the set from click the way the sibling `_commands_offering_json()` already does, instead of writing a literal list.

evidence: Widening `_PortAnswer` with `_Unasked` made `_probe_port`/`_classify` advertise a variant they never produce and broke the provable totality of `_await_startup`'s three-arm match. The agent split the alias into a narrow `_PortAnswer` and a wide `_PortKnowledge`, which is the reviewer's fix with the names swapped.
guidance_note: Before widening a union alias, list every function annotated with it and give the narrower producers their own name rather than redefining the shared alias.

narrative: Three round-0 findings, all on the original diff: an invented symbol in a docstring, a hard-coded command tuple in a test, and an over-widened union alias. The agent fixed all three in one commit, declining only the README-parsing half of F2 because of an owner rule. Round 1 approved with no new findings. The test docstring still carried counts ("All five", "six commands") that later went stale in crom#58.
guidance_observations: The F2 fix removed the literal tuple but left numeric counts in the same test's docstring; sweeping the prose along with the code would have prevented crom#58/F10.
All fixes went out in a single push, so no extra rounds were spent.

evidence: `Tab.title` is `document.title` and `_Version.browser` comes from an unvetted listener, and both reached `click.echo` unsanitised. Fix 5495b0b used `_one_line` for title/url but only bare `printable` for browser/websocket, even though the agent's own reply explained that `printable` keeps newlines, which led to F7-F9.
guidance_note: When adding a stricter sanitiser for one set of foreign fields, apply it to every field parsed at that boundary that renders as one line, not just the fields the finding named.

evidence: The `_probe_option` docstring said "six commands" but still said "five copies ... the sixth command". The agent removed the counts instead of bumping them, but did not sweep the identical counts in the test docstring, which became F10.
guidance_note: When a diff changes how many commands carry a decorator, grep for every spelled-out count ("five", "six", "sixth") across code, tests and docs, and fix them all in one pass.

evidence: This duplicates F1 from the render side. The reviewer asked to wrap at `_tab_lines`/`_browser_facts`; the agent sanitised at the parse site so every consumer holds printable text by construction. That placement is sound, but its execution left browser/websocket on bare `printable` (F7-F9).
guidance_note: Print foreign text in a terminal only after it has passed the line-safe sanitiser at the point where it is parsed.

evidence: The README said `heard` was "the only one of the five that is always filled in", but `status_cmd` builds `processes` from `state.pids` unconditionally, and a later README paragraph already said so; the first sentence was rewritten to carve out `processes`.
guidance_note: When a doc paragraph states which keys can be null, check it against the paragraph that enumerates the same keys and against the record builder before committing.

evidence: The comprehension dropped `page` targets missing title/url, so the tab count was quietly short. The fix made the whole listing `None`, but it gave `_pages_in` a second reason to return `None` while `_lists_targets` still used it as the read loop's completeness predicate (F12), and it typed key presence rather than values (F11). The agent's reply 2 even noted the `_lists_targets` consequence and judged it correct.
guidance_note: When you add a new reason for a function to return None, check every caller that branches on None, especially loop predicates, before shipping.

evidence: Two separate `ps` readings let a reused pid report a stranger's uptime. The agent rejected both a comment and a third `ps` call, and instead scoped `uptimes_on(profile_dir)` to one reading filtered by user-data-dir; the 5495b0b diff and the `UptimeScopeTest` cases show the reused pid comes back absent.
guidance_note: When a reading keyed only by pid is joined to an identity keyed by another reading, key the second reading on the same identity at design time.

evidence: Fix 5495b0b changed `_devtools_version` to `printable(...)` while `_tab_in` got `_one_line`, so newlines in Browser/webSocketDebuggerUrl could still forge output lines; 1874015 switched both to `_one_line`. The agent conceded: "I reasoned about exactly this threat one function away and then did not carry it across." (The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply accepts.)
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a stricter helper for a threat class, grep for every call to the weaker helper on the same boundary and upgrade them in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F7 on the same line of fix commit 5495b0b, where bare `printable(websocket)` kept the newline; the same 1874015 change closed it.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a stricter helper for a threat class, grep for every call to the weaker helper on the same boundary and upgrade them in the same commit.

evidence: This is a third report of the 5495b0b gap: `_Version(printable(...), printable(websocket))` lets a squatting listener inject a forged status line. 1874015 replaced both with `_one_line`, and a forge-a-line test pins it.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a stricter helper for a threat class, grep for every call to the weaker helper on the same boundary and upgrade them in the same commit.

evidence: F2's fix removed the counts from `_probe_option` but left "All five" / "six commands, five of which" / "a sixth command" in the test docstring, which the 1874015 diff removes. The agent: "the same defect as `_probe_option`'s docstring from the last round, in the one place I did not look."
guidance_note: When fixing a stale count, grep the repo for the same number-words around the same concept before pushing, not only the line the reviewer anchored.

evidence: F5's `_tab_in` matched `{"title": title, "url": url}` on key presence, so `null` became the literal "None". The pre-review code had the same hole, so this is the remainder F5's "undescribed page" rule did not cover, not a fresh break; 1874015 types both values with `str() as`.
guidance_note: When writing a rule that a field must describe the page, write the accept/reject table for present-but-null and wrong-type values as well as absent keys before writing the pattern.

evidence: Before 5495b0b, `_pages_in` returned None only for incomplete or non-array JSON. F5's fix added "complete but undescribable", and `_lists_targets` (the `_read_reply` completeness predicate) then waited out `PORT_REPLY_SECONDS` on a held-open socket. 1874015 split out `_listing_in`.
guidance_note: When changing a function's None semantics, read each call site's question, and if a caller asks a narrower question, give it its own predicate in the same commit.

evidence: The `_tab_in` docstring with "`TARGET_LIST_BYTES` refuses a few lines above" was written in F5's fix commit 5495b0b, by which time `TARGET_LIST_BYTES` sat roughly 480 lines higher, so the positional claim was false when written. The flag names 1874015, but that commit did not touch this sentence.
guidance_note: Don't put positional words ("above", "below", "a few lines") in docstrings; name the symbol only.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the README line "which often tells those apart" is in the original diff (hunk @@ -153), and 1874015 did not touch README. The premise holds because `_probe_port` folds `_StillSpeaking` into `_Silent`, so starting up, shutting down and wedged all print one sentence.
guidance_note: Before a doc promises that output distinguishes N causes, trace each cause to the string it produces.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the `_ps` docstring's command list was in the original diff (`_ps` already appears as context in 5495b0b), and 1874015 did not touch it. The list omitted `restart`/`show`, which reach `find_pids` via `kill`/`launch`; the agent took the reviewer's parenthetical and dropped the list.
guidance_note: Don't enumerate callers by command name in a docstring; name the entry functions (`scan`, `find_pids`, `kill`, `launch`) instead.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 1874015 changed only this test's docstring. The missing stub dates from the original PR adding `status` (`uptimes()` already shelled out to `ps`). The agent showed the subtest passes with a booby-trapped `_ps` only once `uptimes_on` is stubbed.
guidance_note: When adding a command to a loop test that stubs every external system, list the new command's external calls and add a stub for each one.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: "both are `null` when nothing answered" is original README text that 5495b0b and 1874015 left alone. The premise holds because `_browser_facts` returns `_nothing_heard` for all of `Unreachable`, including `_AnsweredByStranger`. The law is pasted onto a doc wording fix.
guidance_note: When documenting when a key is null, quote the match arm that produces null and state that arm's condition.

narrative: Round 0 raised six real findings on the new `crom status`. Fix commit 5495b0b caused every round-1 finding: `_one_line` was applied to tab fields but not to the version document (F7-F9), the count sweep missed the test docstring (F10), and the per-page readability rule both missed null values (F11) and broke `_lists_targets` as a loop predicate (F12). It also wrote a positional comment that was already false (F13). Round 2's other four findings were original-PR doc and test gaps that earlier rounds missed. Round 3 approved.
guidance_observations: F1/F3 and F5's fixes each solved the named instance and stopped. Grepping for sibling call sites of the weaker helper and for callers of the changed None contract would have removed round 1 entirely.
In F5 reply 2 the agent noticed the `_lists_targets` consequence and rationalised it as correct; a consequence noticed during a fix deserves a test that exercises it, not a sentence.
Three duplicate threads (F7-F9) for one gap show the reviewer fans out; one consolidated fix was the right response.

evidence: The agent measured `crom down live --all` printing the same "Usage: crom down [OPTIONS] [REF]" and "Try ... --help" lines as click's own `--nosuchflag` error. That matches click attaching the active context to a ctx-less UsageError raised inside a command callback, so the suggested `get_current_context()` changes nothing observable.

Changing `default="default"` to `ref or "default"` made `crom down ""` stop the default profile instead of failing `invalid_name`; the agent reproduced "proj/default was not running exit=0". The fix `"default" if ref is None else ref` landed in 1bb888d, but the promised test was not pushed until d21bcaa (F5).
guidance_note: When removing a click default in favour of an optional None argument, test the explicit-empty-string case before and after, since `or` collapses it into the omitted case.

evidence: The sweep's bare `raise _Failure` carried no reason slug, contradicting the module docstring and README. The agent added a per-row `failure` object built from `_ANSWERS` via a new `_reported` and documented the carve-out, because a single envelope cannot name N failures. The fix did not cover the `unavailable` namespace row (F7).
guidance_note: When a new failure path is added to a command with a documented every-failure-has-a-reason contract, design how it carries the reason before review, not after.

evidence: Round 1 reviewed 1bb888d, which carried only the F2 fix; F3's promised per-row reason landed later in d21bcaa (04:23, after the 04:14 review). So the finding was true of the reviewed commit and exists only because the push held part of the planned fixes.
guidance_note: Push all of a round's planned fixes together; a partial push triggers a review that re-flags every promised fix not yet in the tree.

evidence: 1bb888d, named as F2's fix, had the expression change but not the promised test, which came in d21bcaa as `test_down_refuses_an_empty_ref_rather_than_stopping_the_default_profile`. The reviewer's "exits 3" repeated the agent's own wrong plan comment; the measured exit is 1.
guidance_note: Commit the regression test in the same commit as the fix it pins, and check exit codes against `_ANSWERS` before quoting them in a plan.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the backticked `--all` help string is in the original round-0 hunk, and d21bcaa did not touch it. Click prints option help raw, and the agent confirmed it was the only option help string with backticks and added a click-derived guard.
guidance_note: Write option `help=` strings as plain text, because click renders them verbatim.

evidence: d21bcaa added `failure` to every profile row and README says it is "null everywhere else", but the `{"namespace", "error"}` unavailable row was left without it; the agent admits "I had scoped this out". The agent added `"failure": None` but declined the rename because it matches `crom list --all`'s shape, which is sound.
guidance_note: When adding a key that a doc promises is on every row, enumerate every `records.append` in the function and add it to each, including the ones unreachable today.

narrative: Round 0 found a real empty-ref regression (F2) and a missing reason slug on the sweep (F3), and the agent correctly refuted F1 by measuring click's output. The agent pushed 1bb888d with only the F2 expression change, so round 1 re-flagged the unpushed F3 work (F4) and the unpushed F2 test (F5). The F3 fix in d21bcaa then skipped the unavailable-namespace row (F7), and round 2 also caught an original backtick help string (F6). Round 3 approved.
guidance_observations: Pushing one fix while others were still planned bought a review round whose only findings were the work not yet pushed.
The agent's plan comment published a wrong exit code that the reviewer then echoed; measuring before stating would have kept the record clean.
Adding a schema key across rows without enumerating every row-producing site left a shape hole the reviewer had to find.
